package_info.package_manager: Unknown (likely npm or PyPI based on context)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is explicitly designed to compromise systems by installing a keylogger that exfiltrates all keystrokes to an attacker-controlled webhook, representing an immediate and active threat rather than a passive vulnerability.

execution_context.file_location: main package code (e.g., index.js, main.py, etc.)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code hooks into system keystroke events, captures all user keystrokes, and sends each keystroke to a hardcoded attacker-controlled webhook via HTTP POST, enabling real-time credential and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Keylogging and exfiltration of keystrokes to an external server is a classic malicious behavior with no legitimate use in general-purpose packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages should not monitor user keystrokes or transmit them externally; this is a clear violation of user privacy and security.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Keylogging may be legitimate in accessibility tools or parental control software, but only with explicit user consent and transparency.
key_indicators: Sends keystroke data to external webhook

attack_chain.action: User installs and runs the malicious package, which loads the keylogger component.
Keylogger captures each keystroke and immediately sends it to the attacker's webhook endpoint.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives all victim keystrokes in real time, enabling credential theft and further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Package code that hooks into system keystroke events
Network requests to external domains triggered by user input events
Exfiltration of user input data (keystrokes) to hardcoded webhooks
file_indicators: References to keylogger libraries or modules
Code that registers global keyboard event listeners
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to webhook.site or similar domains
Frequent small POST requests containing keystroke data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that access keyboard events and send data externally, especially to hardcoded or suspicious domains. Flag any package that implements keylogging functionality without clear, legitimate justification. Use static analysis to detect code patterns that register global keyboard listeners and dynamic analysis to observe runtime network exfiltration of user input.
